To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intracellularly localized MePcS(4) (Al and Zn) generate free radicals, which are responsible for their phototoxic effects.

the intracellular generation of radicals by MePcSs depends on the length of incubation of the dye with the cells and that the photocytotoxicity of ZPcS4 is markedly higher than that observed for AlPcS.

tetrasulphonate derivatives of aluminium- and zinc-phthalocyanine are potent photosensitizers of lymphoma cells and that the intracellular generation of reactive oxygen species, in particular free radicals, is involved in the phototoxic process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phototoxic properties of Al- and Zn-tetrasulphonated phthalocyanines and the mechanisms involved in the generation of free radicals in the cells.
the photophysical properties of tetrasubstituted metallo-phthalocyamines and their interaction with cellular components.
a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in the photosensitizing effects of tetrasulpho-phthalocyanine dyes in cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phototoxicity and the formation of intracellular radicals by the MePcS are dependent on the pre-illumination incubating conditions.
the phototoxicity induced by the MePcSs in the lymphoma cell line is mediated by free-radical damage.
the intracellular photoprocesses induced by MePcS 4 involve the formation of free radicals, which are responsible for the photocytotoxicity of MePcS(4) in lymphoid cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photodynamic effects of MePcSs in cells are mediated through the generation of free radicals, and the extent of damage depends on the incubation time and the type of metal.
MePcS(4) are potent photosensitizers of free radical formation, which can lead to cell killing.
the intracellular generation of reactive radicals is the primary photobiological effect of MePcS, which in turn results in cell damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intracellular photoprocesses are not only determined by the chemical nature of the sensitizer, but are also influenced by the pre/post-illuminative incubation time.
, in the case of AlPc and ZnPc, the intracellularly formed free radicals are the main cause of their cytotoxic effects.
, in the presence of cellular oxygen, the intracellularly generated free radicals are the main cause of MePcS-mediated photodamage to cells.
